correctness.rationale: Cauchy--Binet identifies the Plücker quadric on the standard chart with \(F(B)=\det(I_k+BB^{\mathsf T})\). Exact differentiation gives \(\nabla_BF=2\operatorname{adj}(M)B\). Corank at least \(2\) therefore implies singularity; at corank \(1\), writing \(\operatorname{adj}(M)=c\,vv^{\mathsf T}\), gradient vanishing would force \(B^{\mathsf T}v=0\) and hence \(Mv=v\ne0\), a contradiction. The radical-stratum fibration over \(\operatorname{OGr}(r,n)\) gives dimension \(k(n-k)-\binom{r+1}{2}\), so the singular locus has exact codimension \(3\) whenever \(2\le k\le n-2\). The finite checker only replays consequences and is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The initiating paper makes the isotropic-quadric singular codimension a structural input and gives a bound that grows as \(\binom{k+1}{2}\). The accepted theorem replaces that by the exact constant \(3\) in every nontrivial Grassmannian dimension and explains it through the uniform formula \(\operatorname{codim}\Sigma_r=\binom{r+1}{2}\). This is a natural complete stratification of a canonical divisor, not an arbitrary finite slice or a numerical recomputation. The result is useful independently of whether it strengthens the source's separate ED-generality dimension criterion.
